market.title: EU Instant Payments Regulation: Final Countdown for Banks
market.summary_short: European banks are entering the final phase of implementing the EU Instant Payments Regulation, with critical deadlines approaching for receiving and sending instant payments. The regulation aims to make instant payments the norm across the SEPA zone, enhancing liquidity and efficiency for corporates.
market.summary_detail: The EU Instant Payments Regulation, which came into force earlier this year, mandates that all payment service providers (PSPs) in the Eurozone must offer instant credit transfers. The first key deadline, requiring PSPs to be able to *receive* instant payments at no extra cost, is set for early 2027. Subsequently, PSPs must also be able to *send* instant payments within the SEPA area. This regulation is a significant step towards modernizing European payment infrastructure, ensuring funds are available within seconds, 24/7, 365 days a year. For corporates, this means improved cash flow management, real-time reconciliation, and greater flexibility in managing urgent payments. Banks are currently heavily investing in upgrading their systems and processes to ensure full compliance and leverage the new capabilities.
key_points: Regulation mandates instant credit transfers across Eurozone PSPs.
First deadline for receiving instant payments: early 2027.
Instant payments must be offered at no higher cost than standard credit transfers.
Aims for 24/7/365 availability of funds within seconds.
market.rbi_cash_management: This regulation is critical for CMIplus, directly impacting its payment processing capabilities and service offerings in CEE. RBI must ensure its network banks and the CMIplus platform are fully compliant with the receiving and sending mandates by the respective deadlines, offering competitive instant payment solutions to corporate clients.

market.title: PSD3 Proposals Advance: New Era for Open Banking
market.summary_short: The European Commission's proposals for PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation (PSR) are progressing, signaling a new phase for Open Banking and enhanced consumer protection. These legislative changes will significantly impact how banks and third-party providers interact, potentially expanding data access for corporate treasury.
market.summary_detail: The proposed PSD3 and PSR aim to update the existing PSD2 framework, addressing its shortcomings and adapting to new digital payment trends. Key areas of focus include strengthening fraud prevention measures, improving consumer rights, and further developing the Open Banking ecosystem. For corporate treasury, this could mean more sophisticated API-driven services, better integration with ERP/TMS systems, and potentially broader access to account information and payment initiation services across different banks. The proposals also emphasize stronger authentication requirements and clearer rules for data sharing, which could foster greater trust in Open Banking solutions. Banks are preparing for significant system adjustments and strategic shifts to capitalize on the expanded opportunities and meet new compliance requirements.
key_points: PSD3 and PSR proposals are advancing through EU legislative process.
Focus on enhanced fraud prevention and consumer rights.
Potential for expanded Open Banking data access for corporates.
Stronger authentication and clearer data sharing rules expected.
market.rbi_cash_management: PSD3 and PSR are crucial for CMIplus's Open Banking strategy and API development. RBI must closely monitor the legislative progress to ensure CMIplus APIs remain compliant and competitive, offering advanced Open Banking functionalities like VoP and eBAM to corporate clients across CEE.

market.title: AI Revolutionizes Treasury: Advanced Fraud Prevention
market.summary_short: Artificial intelligence is increasingly being adopted in corporate treasury departments to enhance fraud detection and prevention, particularly for real-time and high-volume payments. AI-powered tools offer sophisticated anomaly detection, significantly reducing financial risks for companies.
market.summary_detail: The rise of instant payments and complex payment landscapes has heightened the need for robust fraud prevention. AI and machine learning algorithms are now being integrated into treasury management systems (TMS) and banking platforms to analyze vast amounts of transaction data in real-time. These systems can identify unusual patterns, detect suspicious payment requests, and flag potential fraudulent activities with greater accuracy than traditional rule-based systems. This proactive approach helps corporates protect against various types of fraud, including BEC (Business Email Compromise) and invoice fraud, which are growing concerns. The implementation of AI in treasury not only secures financial operations but also streamlines compliance checks and improves overall operational efficiency by automating risk assessments.
key_points: AI adoption in treasury for fraud detection is growing.
Real-time analysis of transaction data for anomaly detection.
Reduces risks from BEC and invoice fraud.
Enhances operational efficiency and compliance checks.

market.title: EU Finalizes Instant Payments Regulation, PSD3 Looms

market.summary_detail: The European Union's Instant Payments Regulation has been formally approved, requiring all Payment Service Providers (PSPs) in the Eurozone to offer instant credit transfers within 10 seconds, 24/7/365, by early 2027. This includes ensuring charges are no higher than standard credit transfers. The regulation aims to boost financial inclusion and innovation across the bloc. Concurrently, discussions around PSD3 are intensifying, with a focus on strengthening consumer protection, combating fraud, and refining Open Banking frameworks. PSD3 is anticipated to introduce new API standards and potentially revise liability rules for payment initiation and account information services, shaping a more digital and secure payment ecosystem.

market.title: Global ISO 20022 Migration Accelerates, EBICS Adapts for Richer Data
market.summary_short: The global migration to ISO 20022 for payments continues to gain momentum, with major deadlines approaching for cross-border and domestic schemes. EBICS, a key corporate-to-bank channel, is evolving to fully leverage the rich data capabilities of ISO 20022.
market.summary_detail: Financial institutions worldwide are intensifying their efforts to transition to the ISO 20022 messaging standard, driven by upcoming deadlines for SWIFT's cross-border payments and reporting (CBPR+) and various domestic payment systems. This shift promises richer, more structured data, enabling better reconciliation, fraud detection, and liquidity management for corporates. For European corporates, the EBICS standard, particularly versions 2.5 and 3.0, is crucial for secure and efficient communication with banks. The evolution of EBICS is focused on ensuring seamless integration with ISO 20022 messages, allowing corporates to fully benefit from the enhanced data while maintaining the security and reliability of the EBICS channel. This includes supporting new message types and data elements for cash management and reporting.

market.title: PSD3 Proposal Reshapes Open Banking and Payment Security
market.summary_short: The proposed PSD3 and Financial Data Access (FIDA) framework aims to enhance Open Banking, strengthen payment security, and expand data sharing beyond payments. This will significantly impact API strategies for banks and corporates.
market.summary_detail: The European Commission's proposal for PSD3 and the accompanying FIDA regulation signals a major evolution for Open Banking. PSD3 seeks to refine existing PSD2 rules, focusing on improved fraud prevention, stronger consumer rights, and better access to payment systems for non-banks. FIDA, on the other hand, aims to create a broader framework for financial data sharing, extending beyond payment accounts to areas like investments and mortgages. This dual regulatory push will necessitate significant updates to bank APIs, requiring enhanced security protocols, standardized data models, and broader data access capabilities. Corporates will benefit from richer data insights and more integrated financial services, but also face new compliance requirements.

market.title: Tokenised Money Market Funds Revolutionize Corporate Liquidity Management
market.summary_short: Tokenised money market funds (MMFs) are emerging as a transformative tool for corporate liquidity management, offering enhanced efficiency and flexibility. These funds provide instant settlement and fractional ownership, addressing key pain points in traditional cash investment.
market.summary_detail: The advent of tokenised money market funds is set to redefine how corporate treasuries manage their short-term liquidity. By leveraging blockchain or distributed ledger technology, these funds enable instant settlement of investments and redemptions, a significant improvement over the T+1 or T+2 cycles of traditional MMFs. This allows for more dynamic intra-day liquidity management and efficient deployment of idle cash. Furthermore, tokenisation facilitates fractional ownership, making MMFs accessible to a broader range of investors and for smaller investment amounts. Key use cases include optimizing working capital, managing collateral, and providing a more agile alternative for short-term investments, potentially reducing costs and increasing transparency.

They enhance intra-day liquidity management for corporate treasuries.

regulatory.title: Ongoing Evolution of TARGET Services and ISO 20022 Standards
regulatory.summary_short: The ECB continues to oversee the evolution of TARGET Services (T2, T2S, TIPS), which are foundational for euro payments and securities settlement, with ISO 20022 as the underlying messaging standard. Banks must ensure full compliance with these standards for seamless operations.
regulatory.summary_detail: The TARGET Services, including the new generation TARGET2 (T2) for real-time gross settlement, TARGET2-Securities (T2S) for securities settlement, and TARGET Instant Payment Settlement (TIPS), are critical market infrastructures. The migration to T2 completed in March 2023, standardizing all payments on ISO 20022 XML messaging. Ongoing governance and operational requirements necessitate continuous adherence to these standards. Future enhancements and oversight activities will continue to shape the operational landscape for banks, requiring continuous monitoring and adaptation to maintain compliance and efficiency.
key_points: Mandatory use of ISO 20022 XML for all TARGET2 payments.
Continuous adherence to TARGET Services operational rules and governance.
Impact on interbank and corporate payment processing.
Ongoing oversight of payment systems and critical service providers.
regulatory.rbi_cash_management: CMIplus must ensure its payment factory and connectivity channels (EBICS, H2H, SWIFT) fully support ISO 20022 for all euro payments processed via TARGET2. Continuous monitoring of TARGET Services documentation for any operational updates or new technical standards (ITS/RTS) is essential for RBI's network banks in CEE.

regulatory.title: EU Regulations on Instant Payments, PSD3, PSR Impact Liquidity Management
regulatory.summary_short: A new EBA report details the significant impact of the Instant Payments Regulation (IPR), proposed PSD3, and Payment Services Regulation (PSR) on liquidity management for financial institutions. These regulations will accelerate instant payment adoption and necessitate changes in how banks manage their liquidity.
regulatory.summary_detail: The Euro Banking Association (EBA) Liquidity Management Working Group (LMWG) has published a report analyzing the profound implications of three key EU regulatory initiatives: the Instant Payments Regulation (IPR), the proposed Payment Services Regulation (PSR), and the proposed Payment Services Directive 3 (PSD3). The report highlights how these measures are expected to drive the widespread adoption of instant payments, fostering a more level playing field among market participants. Consequently, financial institutions will need to significantly adapt their liquidity management strategies and systems to cope with the increased velocity and 24/7 nature of instant payment flows. This includes ensuring sufficient funding for continuous settlement and managing intraday liquidity more dynamically. The report serves as a crucial guide for banks to prepare for these transformative changes.
key_points: Instant Payments Regulation (IPR) mandates 24/7 instant payment processing, requiring continuous liquidity.
Proposed PSD3/PSR aims to enhance payment security, consumer protection, and open banking, impacting payment flows and data access.
Banks must adapt systems for real-time, continuous liquidity monitoring, forecasting, and funding.
Regulations promote a level playing field, potentially increasing competition and requiring strategic adjustments.
regulatory.rbi_cash_management: RBI CMIplus must assess the impact on its liquidity management capabilities, especially for instant payment processing across its CEE network banks. This includes evaluating real-time liquidity reporting, forecasting, and funding mechanisms to ensure continuous availability for instant payment settlement, and preparing for API-driven liquidity data access under PSD3/PSR.
regulatory.regulation_area: Instant Payments, PSD3, Liquidity Management, Open Banking

regulatory.title: EBA Updates Fraud Taxonomy to Version 7.0, Effective January 2027
regulatory.summary_short: The EBA has released version 7.0 of its Fraud Taxonomy, effective 1 January 2027, updating classifications to reflect the latest fraud trends. This taxonomy provides a harmonised framework for classifying payment fraud, crucial for compliance with the forthcoming Payment Services Regulation.
regulatory.summary_detail: The Euro Banking Association (EBA) has issued version 7.0 of its EBA Fraud Taxonomy, which will become effective on 1 January 2027. This annual review, supported by fraud experts across Europe, ensures the taxonomy remains relevant to evolving fraud trends. Key updates in version 7.0 include replacing 'emotional manipulation' with more specific modi like 'support a friend or family member fraud', 'romance fraud', and 'charity / donation fraud'. Additionally, new labels have been added for suspected money mule activity and 'card chip relay' fraud. The taxonomy provides a standardised pan-European vocabulary and categorisation approach for all payment-related fraud scenarios, enhancing fraud monitoring, reporting, and information sharing, particularly in anticipation of information-sharing arrangements under the forthcoming Payment Services Regulation (PSR).
key_points: Version 7.0 of the EBA Fraud Taxonomy takes effect on 1 January 2027.
Updated classifications include new specific fraud modi (e.g., romance fraud, charity fraud).
New labels added for suspected money mule activity and 'card chip relay' fraud.
Designed to support harmonised fraud data sharing and reporting requirements under the forthcoming Payment Services Regulation (PSR).
regulatory.rbi_cash_management: RBI CMIplus needs to ensure its fraud detection and reporting systems are updated to align with EBA Fraud Taxonomy version 7.0 by January 2027. This involves reviewing and adapting internal fraud classification logic, data capture, and reporting mechanisms to comply with the new standards and facilitate information sharing as required by the upcoming Payment Services Regulation.
regulatory.regulation_area: Payment Services Regulation (PSR), Fraud Prevention, Compliance
